cover.title:
ACME CUSTOMER PORTAL
WALKING DECK
cover.subtitle: One self-service view of the program, readable in 10-20 minutes
cover.notes: A walking deck is a self-service story a newcomer can read without a presenter.

agenda.title: THE STORY IN 10-20 MINUTES
agenda.takeaway: Told like a news story: the need, the solution, how it works, and where we go next.

items.head: WHY CHANGE
items.body: The business context, the pain, and the cost of the status quo

items.head: THE SOLUTION
items.body: One operating model that standardizes and scales

items.head: HOW IT WORKS
items.body: The delivery lifecycle and each team's clear job

problem.title: WHY WE'RE HERE: ONE TRUSTED CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE
problem.takeaway: Customer data and journeys are scattered across tools, creating cost, rework, and inconsistent service.

context.label: WHO WE SERVE
context.text: Acme customer-facing teams (support, sales, success). What they care about: fast, consistent, compliant service - one view of the customer, everywhere.

cards.head: FRAGMENTED TOOLS
bullets: Data lives in CRM, tickets, and spreadsheets.

cards.head: BUSINESS IMPACT
bullets: Leaders can't see the whole picture.

problem.source: Confirm objectives and success measures with the sponsor.
problem.notes: So what: today the same work is done many times and customers get inconsistent service.

vision.title: THE OPERATING MODEL: STANDARDIZE ONCE, REUSE EVERYWHERE
vision.takeaway: One governed path reduces cost and gives every team the same trusted customer view.
vision.label: OPERATING MODEL
vision.statement: Every interaction follows one visible, repeatable path - capture, govern, serve, and measure.

steps.head: TRUSTED SOURCE
steps.body: One system of record for the customer.

steps.head: ACTIVATED SERVICE
steps.body: The same view reaches every channel.

vision.sowhat: The so-what:  lower cost (do it once)   •   higher trust (one version)   •   faster service (governed reuse).
vision.notes: Lead with the why: standardization reduces cost and eliminates multiple versions of the truth.

how_it_works.title: HOW IT WORKS: GOVERNANCE TRAVELS WITH THE WORK
how_it_works.takeaway: Each stage adds a control that protects quality, compliance, and findability.
how_it_works.governance: Single owner, validated once, consistent data, controlled routing, scoped access, and measured outcomes - so leaders always know the state of the work.
how_it_works.notes: Spell out the governance benefit of each step in plain language.

roles.title: EACH TEAM HAS ONE CLEAR JOB
roles.takeaway: Clear ownership is the win: one intake, one source, many service channels.
roles.footnote: Channels: web, phone, email, chat, and partner portals.
roles.source: Ownership maps back to the pain points: cost, trust, and scale.
roles.notes: Standardize the categories across all cards so the audience compares like-for-like.

roadmap.title: THE ROADMAP: PROVE IT, THEN SCALE
roadmap.takeaway: We are here - Phase 1 launches now; Phase 2 follows; the model then scales.

waves.head: PHASE 1  ·  SUPPORT
waves.body: Support intake and system of record live and stabilized.

waves.head: ENABLERS
waves.body: Shared data model and governance establish the path.

waves.head: PHASE 2  ·  SALES
waves.body: Apply the proven cycle to sales, then success.

roadmap.outcome: Support live  •  Governance embedded  •  Sales integrated  •  Success onboarded
roadmap.notes: Start the timeline section here, then drill into the current phase.

milestones.title: PHASE 1 (SUPPORT): DELIVERY MILESTONES
milestones.takeaway: Discovery and build are done; launch is near; integration and retirement close out the year.
milestones.critical_path: Critical path:  data + access  ->  validation  ->  governed service  ->  integration  ->  retirement
milestones.source: High-level dates; task-level detail lives in the plan.
milestones.notes: Merge delivery phases and roadmap into one dated view.

current_state.title: WHERE WE ARE NOW: BUILD DONE, LAUNCH AMBER
current_state.takeaway: A level-set: build is complete; launch and validation are the active work.
current_state.mode: CURRENT MODE  |  Validate the flow, close data and access exceptions, enable users, and prepare retirement.
current_state.notes: Keep it honest: launch is near, closure remains amber until validation lands.

team.title: DELIVERY DEPENDS ON SHARED OWNERSHIP
team.takeaway: Business, platform, service operations, and program controls move as one team.
team.notes: The easy slide. Names tie the model to accountable owners.

next_steps.title: FINISH THE FLOW, THEN MAKE IT DURABLE
next_steps.takeaway: The immediate ask is disciplined closure of Phase 1 - not another redesign.

moves.action: Confirm data load and access reconciliation.
Close data and access exceptions under change control.
Complete training, docs, and support coverage.
Integrate sales and plan legacy retirement.

help: One intake, one record, many channels.
Maintain support until evidence supports closure.
next_steps.success: SUCCESS = ONE TRUSTED CUSTOMER VIEW, AT SCALE
next_steps.notes: Close on the ask: finish Phase 1 cleanly, then repeat.

closer.title: SALES IS NEXT - AND THE MODEL SCALES
closer.takeaway: Prove it with support, repeat with sales, then extend to every team.

tiers.head: PHASE 1  ·  SUPPORT
tiers.body: First team migrated, integrated, and stabilized.

tiers.head: PHASE 2  ·  SALES
tiers.body: The same cycle applied to sales.

tiers.head: PHASE 3+  ·  SCALE
tiers.body: Success, partners, and more - one team at a time.

closer.banner: One trusted source   ·   Standardize once   ·   Reuse everywhere
closer.notes: Leave the audience with one message: the value is the repeatable model.
